text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Analysts impressed by Unilever chairman Niall FitzGerald on tour of US investment houses. Stock up to highest ever. (p1)
- Construction firm Heijmans reports flat first-half earnings, shares one of the biggest losers on the bourse. (p1)
- Schiphol Airport Authority expresses disappointment over new fifth runway delay. Now due to be completed in 2003/4. (p4)
- Talks between Fokker and Korea's Samsung due to come to a head within a week. Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers says Samsung's business plan is not specific enough yet. (p1)
- Groningen court rules that takeover of timber group Houtgroep NEderland by rival Eecen can go ahead. (p3)
- Netherlands has not got back gold from Switzerland stolen by the Nazis. (p1)
- Energy companies call for the closing of coal-powered genrators. (p15)
- Workers in the Dutch hotel and catering industry oppose smoking ban. (p15)
- Samsung will give Fokker no guarantee that jobs will not be lost in any takeover. (p27)
- Bankers Kempen & Co have introduced a new fund, the Orange Midcap Fund, which will invest in the 43 or so medium-sized firms with a quote on the Amsterdam bourse (p29)
- Simac, the information technology company based in Veldhoven, sees a 45 percent jump in first half profits. (p27)
- Limburg energy distribution company Mega Limburg up for sale. Germany's Ruhrgas interested. (p11)
- In the Dutch metal industry a 36-hour week remains an illusion. (p11)
